title: Calling All Creators: Join Our EveryWear Specialist Program
content:
Are you a skilled fashion creator ready to bring virtual garments to life in gaming?

title: Silicone/Rubber dipped drawstring
content:
Does anyone have any tips on how to create this silicone rubber texture in CLO?   
I have already made the drastring, just need help with the texture! :)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/fe8425513b88465f804aa7dd8df14ba9/images/2f21ef308f6e42c8b2167dfb6c1e7633Hoodie-Cord-with-Coated-Silicone.png)


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you for your comments! I will do my best :)

Comment 2: I did a close study but unfortunately I can't post a photo from here. You shouldn't think like a pattern, you should think like a 3D solid object in CLO. It will consist of 4 piecesStepsFabric: Plastic1. Draw a circle for the bottom pieceWidth: 1.7 cmHight1.7 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 102. Draw a circle for the top pieceWidth: 1.5 cmHight 1.5 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 103. Draw a circle for the middle large pieceWidth: 2.5 cmHight 2.5 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %100Resolution 104. Draw a circle for the middle small pieceWidth: 1.8 cmHight 1.8 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature 100%Resolution 10Add UV PackagingExport obj (thick)Import obj (Select Trim)Material PlasticSave Trim
Reply 1: Hello, I'm Robin, the Product Manager at CONNECT.We'll work on improving the platform so you can post images in comments for a better communication experience.

Comment 3: Cut the end part you want to make silicone and separate the cord. Delete the cord. There should be no texture in the remaining part. Export as obj. Then add it to your file as trim and choose plastic as material. If not, I think you can try to make your obj file look like this in blender.

Comment 4: Hi, I've tried two options, both of which were unsatisfactory. Using a displacement map doesn't create this look (the knot is still "comparted" and not "coated") and trying to wrap a pattern piece around the knotted part and shrink that in so that it causes the "coated" effect also didn't work. So if anyone else has an idea?
Reply 1: I did a close study but unfortunately I can't post a photo from here. You shouldn't think like a pattern, you should think like a 3D solid object in CLO. It will consist of 4 piecesStepsFabric: Plastic1. Draw a circle for the bottom pieceWidth: 1.7 cmHight1.7 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 102. Draw a circle for the top pieceWidth: 1.5 cmHight 1.5 cmTchickness 50 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %20Resolution 103. Draw a circle for the middle large pieceWidth: 2.5 cmHight 2.5 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature %100Resolution 104. Draw a circle for the middle small pieceWidth: 1.8 cmHight 1.8 cmTchickness 30 mmParticle distance 1 mmCurvature 100%Resolution 10Add UV PackagingExport obj (thick)Import obj (Select Trim)Material PlasticSave Trim
